intent: Read the GEO count table (one row per gene, one column per cell, first column holds the gene names) and run basic quality control: keep cells with at least 5 detected genes and genes detected in at least 3 cells, then save neural_qc.h5ad.
silent_error: scanpy.read_csv (like anndata.io.read_csv) always returns rows as observations and columns as variables (the AnnData obs x var convention); it has no way to know that this table is genes x cells, and its docstring says nothing about orientation. Without a transpose the 'cells' of the AnnData are the genes and the 'genes' are the cells, so filter_cells/filter_genes silently apply the cell filter to genes and the gene filter to cells. Exit 0, valid h5ad, no message.

files.neural_qc.py:
import scanpy as sc

adata = sc.read_csv("GSE250001_raw_counts.csv")
sc.pp.filter_cells(adata, min_genes=5)
sc.pp.filter_genes(adata, min_cells=3)
adata.write_h5ad("neural_qc.h5ad")

import scanpy as sc
